payload.text: The Brennecke Institute developed a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery intended to reduce negative-electrolyte crossover, a key aging mechanism in sodium-flow systems. Independent auditing corrected the prototype’s cycle life to 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity knee; the earlier 12,000-cycle claim was retracted because it used un-normalized depth-of-discharge. The chemistry delivers 148 Wh/kg gravimetric energy density and has a projected stack-level cost of $61/kWh at 500 MWh manufacturing scale. Its operational limitation is a 4 °C temperature floor, below which the thalliline dopant precipitates and cycling must stop.
